# ninesixteen.video — full product reference

## One-line summary

ninesixteen.video is a native Windows screen recorder for true 9×16 portrait and 16×9 landscape capture. Frame with your cursor, zoom with Alt + scroll, use Game mode for fixed-frame gameplay, and export MP4 with a one-time $49 Pro license.

## Who it is for

- TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts creators who want vertical clips without cropping
- Gamers and reviewers who need a locked full-frame capture with system cursor
- Founders and product teams recording SaaS demos in 9×16 or 16×9
- Tutorial and course creators who need tight UI framing
- Anyone who wants native aspect ratio screen recording on Windows without OBS scene setup

## Core features

1. **True 9×16 and 16×9 capture** — Pick portrait or landscape in Studio. Overlay, library player, and exports match your format. No letterboxing, no crop step in post.
2. **Cursor-driven framing** — The viewport follows your mouse. Alt + scroll zooms from full desktop into a tight crop live while recording.
3. **Game mode** — Locks full 9×16 or 16×9 with zoom disabled. Portrait: Crosshair (centered) or Cursor (horizontal pan only). Uses system cursor, not cinematic pointer.
4. **Rule-of-thirds guides** — Compose shots intentionally mid-recording.
5. **System + microphone audio** — Blend desktop sound and voice with gain meters.
6. **Optional mouse click audio** — Mix click SFX into recordings (Studio toggle + volume).
7. **Encrypted local recordings** — Stored on your machine; nothing uploads until you export.
8. **Native Windows Graphics Capture** — Lightweight Tauri app, FFmpeg bundled.
9. **Virtual camera** — Device name "ninesixteen.video" in OBS, Zoom, Google Meet.
10. **Quality ladder** — Portrait up to 1080p @ 30/60 fps. Landscape 720p through 4K @ 30/60 fps (1440p and 4K @ 60 fps with Pro).
11. **Hardware-aware Studio** — Recommends resolution and fps your PC can encode reliably.
12. **Adaptive H.264** — NVENC, AMD AMF, Intel QSV, or software fallback.
13. **In-app library** — Preview takes, filmstrip thumbnails, slide-out player.

## Pricing

| Tier | Price | Includes |
|------|-------|----------|
| Free | $0 | Record, preview, all capture features |
| Pro | $49 USD one-time | Unlimited MP4 export to disk or Google Drive |

No subscription. No renewals.

## System requirements

- Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit)
- WebView2 (installer bootstraps if needed)
- 8 GB RAM minimum, 16 GB recommended
- DirectX 11 GPU, 2 GB VRAM
- 1920×1080 display or higher
- ~500 MB disk for app; SSD recommended for recordings

## How it differs from OBS

OBS records full desktop or manual regions — you reframe for vertical social. ninesixteen records native 9×16 or 16×9 from frame one with cursor follow and Game mode. OBS is better for live streaming and complex multi-source setups. ninesixteen is faster for native-aspect clips and one-time Pro export.

## Latest release — v1.2.0 (June 2026)

- Game mode — locked full frame, portrait Crosshair or Cursor pan, system cursor
- 4K landscape @ 60 fps and 1440p landscape @ 60 fps — Pro export
- Hardware-aware quality caps in Studio
- Adaptive H.264 — NVENC, AMF, QSV, software fallback
- Tier limits from RAM, CPU threads, and GPU VRAM

## Previous release — v1.1.0 (June 2026)

- 16×9 landscape recording in Studio
- Cinematic cursor overhaul

- Faster Library and smarter viewport panning
- 720p @ 30fps defaults
